text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bund futures held early gains in exceptionally light trade with dealers aiming to keep the German market closely linked to Treasury prices which were stable ahead of a U.S. holiday. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.52, up 0.29 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts drifted higher, relieved by only a modest rise in British producer prices in October, which left the year-on-year core rate at a 30-year low. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-13/32, up 14/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - The French bond market was closed for Armistice Day. On Friday, December bond futures suffered a late sell-off, closing down 0.08 basis points at 127.20, as local traders closed positions ahead of the long weekend. Traders said they expected the contract to remain range-bound this week.

ITALY - Debt markets ended softer after a subdued day which traders described as "boring, boring, boring," with U.S. markets closed for a holiday. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 125.68, down 0.03 from Friday's settlement price.
UNITED STATES - The U.S. Treasury market is closed today for the Veteran's Day holiday in the United States. The market will resume trading on Tuesday.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese government bond contract ended with substantial losses on corrective selling led by city banks. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 123.51, down 0.25 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity was subdued as many countries took a day off to remember war veterans,including the U.S., France and Belgium. A handful of sterling floating-rate notes surfaced. S-E-Banken launched a 100 million stg perpetual FRN and Portman Building Society a 150 million three-year FRN. ABN Amro lead managed a 1.2 billion Swedish crown asset-backed bond secured by housing loans. South Africa's Eskom delayed roadshows for a 200 million mark five-year bond.
